prompt: The September Declaration has a rough equivalent in the Netherlands that takes place on the same day every year. In what century was the current name of this day (as of August 2024) chosen?
answer: The current name **“Prinsjesdag” was chosen in the 19th century**. It originally referred to the 18th-century celebration of Stadholder William V’s birthday; the name was later applied to the annual opening of Parliament, probably in the latter half of the 19th century. (It was officially associated with that event by the 1930s.)
